Public Comment Supporting Independent Audit Request — Docket 59475, Item 6571
The STOP the Riesel Data Center Coalition supports Kevin Kennedy and John M. Burrow’s request in Item 6571 for an
independent technical investigation and forensic audit of the modeling underlying the 2024 Permian Basin Reliability Plan.

Before further irreversible commitments are made, we ask the Commission to obtain an independent evaluation of the
modeling assumptions, reconcile material differences between the PBRP and the 2024 Regional Transmission Plan, and
publicly explain whether each proposed 765-kV import path remains justified.

We also support the requested pause while that work is completed and reviewed. Our support for an audit does not
presume misconduct or a predetermined result. It reflects the importance of getting decisions of this scale right.

We submit this comment not only as Texans concerned about statewide transmission planning, but also as members of
STOP the Riesel Data Center — a community group directly affected by large-scale energy and infrastructure decisions.
Our experience raises additional concerns that make independent verification even more necessary.

Specifically, our community has been seeking answers about how two former ERCOT employees were permitted to be
hired by Cipher Digital, a company pursuing multiple data-center developments in Texas, including in our area. From our
perspective, this raises serious questions about conflicts of interest, the integrity of planning assumptions, and whether
Texans’ public-interest protections are being upheld.

Our group submitted a formal request for review to Attorney General Ron Paxton on June 26, 2026, asking his office to
investigate this potential ethics violation. We have not received any response. When the same individuals who helped shape
ERCOT’s planning processes later appear in private-sector roles tied to projects dependent on those same planning
outcomes, Texans deserve transparency.

These concerns do not accuse ERCOT or the Commission of wrongdoing. They simply underscore why independent
verification is essential. When billions of dollars, thousands of acres of private land, and long-term ratepayer obligations are
at stake, Texans need confidence that the underlying models are accurate, unbiased, and compliant with all applicable
standards.

For these reasons, we respectfully urge the Commission to grant the request for an independent technical investigation and
forensic audit, and to pause further action on the 765-kV import paths until that work is complete.

Texans deserve clarity before irreversible decisions are made.

STOP the Riesel Data Center Partnership
